subject: jc-english
name: English (Junior Cycle)
note: Draft taxonomy for the current JUNIOR CYCLE English specification (NCCA 2015, amended 2018; first examined 2017). Built on the spec's THREE official strands (Oral Language, Reading, Writing); subtopics are the examinable content areas the FINAL EXAM covers, each traceable to the spec's learning outcomes / prescribed material (DES Circular 0014/2022). Oral Language is included for spec fidelity though it is assessed mainly via CBA 1, not the written exam. specRef cites the spec (/tmp/jc_english_spec.txt) or the prescribed-material requirement. VERIFIED 2026-06-10 by a 4-lens adversarial panel (spec fidelity, HL+OL exam coverage 2023-2024, completeness) + critic: 4/4 pass, 0 blockers, 2 specRef-precision fixes applied. specRefs name cohort-volatile prescribed-text lists for provenance only — they are NOT in curriculum.ts (which stores id+name).

strands.name: Oral Language
strands.specRef: spec p.9 'the three strands: Oral Language, Reading, and Writing' — Strand 1 Oral Language (assessed mainly via CBA 1 Oral Communication; included for fidelity)

subtopics.name: Spoken Communication and Presentation
subtopics.specRef: Oral Language LOs on communicating as a speaker — presenting, speaking with control of register and purpose

subtopics.name: Discussion, Debate and Persuasion
subtopics.specRef: Oral Language LOs on discussion, persuading, responding to others in talk

subtopics.name: Influence and Register of Spoken Language
subtopics.specRef: Oral Language element 'Understanding the content and structure of language' — how spoken language varies by audience/purpose/register

strands.name: Reading
strands.specRef: spec — Strand 2 Reading (Reading/engaging with texts, Comprehending, Responding); the written exam's comprehension + studied-text sections

subtopics.name: Reading Comprehension (Unseen Texts)
subtopics.specRef: Reading LOs on comprehending unseen literary, non-literary and MULTIMODAL stimulus material (exam Section B / comprehension questions)

subtopics.name: Studied Fiction (Novel and Short Story)
subtopics.specRef: prescribed material: two studied novels + short stories (DES Circular); Reading LOs on responding to studied prose

subtopics.name: Studied Drama and Shakespeare
subtopics.specRef: prescribed material: studied drama; HL ONLY studies a full Shakespeare play (Note 2, spec) from the prescribed list; exam Section A often a Shakespeare/drama extract. NB: the prescribed play/film lists are cohort-refreshed — check the current SEC circular per exam year

subtopics.name: Poetry (Studied and Unseen)
subtopics.specRef: prescribed material: >=16 studied poems; exam tests studied + unseen poetry

subtopics.name: Film Studies
subtopics.specRef: prescribed material: one studied film from the prescribed list (Sing Street, Kes, Hotel Rwanda, etc.); exam tests the studied film as a text

subtopics.name: Responding to Texts (Theme, Character, Author's Craft)
subtopics.specRef: Reading LOs 6-8 under the 'Exploring and using language' element (LO6 character/setting/plot; LO7 value judgements on key moments/character/scene; LO8 author's word choice / figurative language / language patterns)

strands.name: Writing
strands.specRef: spec — Strand 3 Writing (composing for purpose/audience; exam's writing tasks across all three sections)

subtopics.name: Functional and Transactional Writing
subtopics.specRef: Writing LOs on writing for a real purpose/audience — speech, letter, report, review, blog, article, instructions (the exam's functional-writing tasks)

subtopics.name: Personal and Creative Writing
subtopics.specRef: Writing LOs on personal, imaginative and creative composition (story, descriptive, personal essay)

subtopics.name: Writing About Studied Texts
subtopics.specRef: Writing + Reading LOs — composing a developed response to a studied novel/play/poem/film (the studied-text written answers in Sections A/C)

subtopics.name: Language, Grammar and Structure
subtopics.specRef: Writing element 'Understanding the content and structure of language' — accuracy of grammar, spelling, punctuation, paragraphing and structuring a piece
